name: Latanoprost
route_note: one eye drop in the evening once daily
originator: Pharmacia (Johan Stjernschantz, Bahram Resul) based on Columbia University work by Laszlo Bito

discovery.by: Laszlo Bito (Columbia University) and Pharmacia researchers
discovery.note: Bito showed that topical prostaglandins lower intraocular pressure; Pharmacia designed a selective, better-tolerated isopropyl ester prodrug of a PGF2-alpha analogue.

tagline: Once-daily prostaglandin eye drop that became first-line for glaucoma
summary: Latanoprost is an isopropyl ester prodrug of a prostaglandin F2-alpha analogue that lowers intraocular pressure by increasing aqueous outflow. Once-daily drops became first-line therapy for open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension. It can permanently darken the iris and lengthen eyelashes.
mechanism: After instillation, corneal esterases hydrolyse latanoprost to latanoprost acid, a selective agonist of the prostaglandin FP receptor.

FP receptor activation in the ciliary muscle remodels the extracellular matrix through matrix metalloproteinases, increasing uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humour and lowering intraocular pressure by roughly a quarter to a third, with effect lasting over 24 hours.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Xalatan approved as the first prostaglandin analogue for glaucoma.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic latanoprost launches in the US after patent expiry.

history.title: Nitric oxide-donating analogue
history.detail: FDA approves latanoprostene bunod (Vyzulta), which adds a nitric oxide-donating moiety.

history.title: Benzalkonium-free emulsion
history.detail: FDA approves Xelpros, a latanoprost emulsion without benzalkonium chloride preservative.

pk.metabolism: hydrolysis by corneal esterases; hepatic beta-oxidation

facts: Its eyelash-growing effect led to the related prostaglandin bimatoprost being marketed as a cosmetic product (Latisse).
